name: Rubber Band AI
description: Keeps AI racers inside a believable gap of the player by scaling their pace, never by teleporting them. It exists because racing against a void is boring and racing against perfect drivers is humiliating; the band is what makes midfield battles happen at any skill level. This component owns only the handicap calculation — it reads race position from world.checkpointCrossed and world.lapCompleted (progress facts owned by world.track_circuit) and emits a pace multiplier. It does not drive the cars: the multiplier lands on the AI vehicle's movement.vehicle_tuning parameters, so a boosted rival obeys the same physics as the player and can still be out-braked into a corner. Difficulty selection is deliberately just the band width; there is no hidden skill model here.

inputs.name: maxGapSeconds
inputs.description: Time gap to the player beyond which the band pulls. This is the difficulty knob — narrower bands produce relentless packs, wider bands let a strong player break away.

inputs.name: catchUpFactor
inputs.description: Pace multiplier applied to AI behind the band. Kept modest so the catch-up reads as pressure, not as a car materializing in the mirror.

inputs.name: fallBackFactor
inputs.description: Pace multiplier applied to AI ahead of the band. Below 1.0 so a dominant player still gets a race in the mirrors.

inputs.name: updateIntervalSeconds
inputs.description: How often handicaps are recomputed. Coarse updates are fine — per-frame adjustment makes the band visible as speed pulsing.

outputs.name: currentHandicaps
outputs.description: Racer id to active pace multiplier. Exposed for telemetry and difficulty-tuning review, not for gameplay reads.
